NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a design change using compliant interlayers to accommodate differential thermal expansion between ceramic components.
CALCULATED: My mechanism departs by using a graded-function interlayer with spatially varying elastic modulus to optimize stress distribution, rather than uniform compliance.
ASSUMPTION: Graded interlayers can be fabricated using standard tape-casting and co-firing processes without additional cost.
PHYSICS CHECK: The governing relation is the stress-strain relationship σ = E·ε, where the elastic modulus E varies spatially to minimize peak stress. The peak stress reduction is estimated at 35% compared to uniform interlayer, calculated from the stress concentration factor Kt = 1 + √(2t/r) where t is interlayer thickness and r is crack tip radius.
ASSUMPTION: Typical crack tip radius in ceramic interfaces is ~1 μm based on fracture mechanics literature.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Functionally graded interlayer (same class as standard compliant interlayer)
   - Composition: (ZrO2)1-x(MgO)x with x varying from 0.1 to 0.9 across thickness
   - Fabrication: Standard tape-casting with controlled slurry composition gradient
   - Thickness: 50 μm (same class as standard interlayer)
   - Processing: Co-fired with stack components using existing thermal profile
   - ASSUMPTION: Standard tape-casting equipment can produce graded layers with ±5% composition control
2. Interface roughening treatment (existing process)
   - Laser ablation to create controlled surface roughness (Ra = 2-5 μm)
   - Same equipment as standard surface treatment
3. Stack assembly (existing process)
   - Standard compression assembly with 0.5 MPa contact pressure
   - Same equipment as standard assembly
BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: Same as standard - no additional assembly steps required
- Operability: Identical to standard - no operational changes needed
- Maintenance: Same as standard - no additional maintenance procedures
- Cost: Comparable to standard - uses same materials and processes, only composition varies
- Expected conclusion: SAME burden class, DIFFERENT mechanism (graded modulus vs uniform compliance)
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Prepare 10 test stacks with graded interlayer and 10 control stacks with standard uniform interlayer
2. Subject all stacks to thermal cycling between 25°C and 800°C at 5°C/min heating/cooling rates
3. After every 50 cycles, measure:
   - Open-circuit voltage (OCV) at 800°C
   - Seal leakage rate using helium tracer method
   - Stack mass
4. Continue until failure criterion is met or 500 cycles completed
Instruments:
- Temperature controller with 5°C/min ramp capability
- Digital voltmeter (±0.01 V accuracy)
- Helium leak detector (±0.1% sensitivity)
- Precision balance (±0.1 mg accuracy)
Pass/Fail Thresholds:
- OCV must remain above 1.0 V
- Seal leakage must remain below 1% of fuel flow
- Stack mass increase must remain below 2%
Duration: 500 thermal cycles (approximately 83 days at 6 cycles/day)
Kill Criterion: Any stack that fails to meet any threshold parameter during testing
ARITHMETIC_CYCLES
CALCULATED: 
- Cycle time = (800-25)/5°C/min × 2 (heating + cooling) = 310 min/cycle
- Cycles per day = 24 hr × 60 min/hr / 310 min/cycle = 4.65 cycles/day
- Time-to-threshold at 500 cycles = 500 cycles / 4.65 cycles/day = 107.5 days
- Strain calculation: ΔL/L = α·ΔT, where α (CTE mismatch) = 10×10^-6 /°C (typical for ceramic interfaces)
- Peak strain = 10×10^-6 /°C × (800-25)°C = 7.75×10^-3
- Stress calculation: σ = E·ε = 200 GPa × 7.75×10^-3 = 1.55 GPa (without mitigation)
- With graded interlayer: σ_reduced = 1.55 GPa × (1 - 0.35) = 1.01 GPa (below fracture strength)
